pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: DIGITAL STORIES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What role do pictures in a book or cover play in a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text
2. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text
3. answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: DIGITAL STORIES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: DIGITAL STORIES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create mental images from viewed, heard or read text

What this means
In this part you learn to create mental images from viewed, heard or read text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create mental images from viewed, heard or read text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create mental images from viewed, heard or read text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories to a partner. (skill: create mental images from viewed, heard or read text)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text.
3. Practise this skill: create mental images from viewed, heard or read text.
4. Practise this skill: answer direct and inferential questions correctly for comprehension.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What role do pictures in a book or cover play in a story?
2. How are digital stories different from story books?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: Digital Stories means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify words, phrases and proverbs from a digital text.
5. Be able to: create mental images from viewed, heard or read text.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
